title: China gold market update: Q3 ends with strong official gold buying
gist: China's central bank bought 23t of gold in September 2026, its biggest monthly purchase since October 2023, taking Q3 buying to 63t and holdings to 2,410t. Chinese gold ETFs hit a record 304t and are on pace for a record inflow year as local equities slump. Meanwhile wholesale (SGE) demand was 234t in Q3, 44% below the ten-year average, because jewellery is weak, and gold fell 8.5% in USD in September on rising US yields and a stronger dollar.

themes.theme: Q3 gold price: yields and dollar vs geopolitics

insights.claim: In September 2026 the LBMA Gold Price PM in USD fell 8.5% and the Shanghai Benchmark Gold Price PM (SHAUPM) in RMB fell 5.5%.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: September's sharp pullback erased much of the quarter's gains and created a dip-buying entry point in China.
insights.quote: with the LBMA Gold Price PM in USD and the SHAUPM in RMB falling 8.5% and 5.5%, respectively.
insights.locator: Gold’s September decline trimmed Q3 gain

insights.claim: The World Gold Council's gold return attribution model (GRAM) attributes gold's September 2026 decline to soaring US Treasury yields amid Fed tightening and a strengthening US dollar.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Real-rate and dollar moves, not physical demand, were the dominant short-term headwind for gold.
insights.quote: soaring US Treasury yields amid the Fed’s tightening moves and the strengthening dollar weighed on gold
insights.locator: Gold’s September decline trimmed Q3 gain

insights.claim: When the US dollar appreciates, the USD-denominated international gold price generally performs worse than gold priced in other currencies, which is why the RMB gold price fell less than the USD price in September 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Currency translation means local-currency gold holders in China were partly cushioned from the USD gold drawdown.
insights.quote: As the dollar appreciates, the international gold price denominated in USD is generally weaker than in other currencies.
insights.locator: Gold’s September decline trimmed Q3 gain

insights.claim: The RMB gold price ended Q3 2026 with a 3% gain, trimming its year-to-date loss to 7%.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Despite a strong Q3, gold in RMB remains down on the year, unusual against heavy official and ETF buying.
insights.quote: The RMB gold price ended Q3 with a 3% gain, trimming its y-t-d loss to 7%.
insights.locator: Gold’s September decline trimmed Q3 gain

insights.claim: The intensifying US-Iran conflict kept inflation concerns elevated and raised expectations of further Fed hikes after a 25bp rate rise in September 2026; combined with resilient US growth this sent short-term US Treasury yields surging, while long-term yields rose mainly on fiscal concerns via term premia.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Geopolitics is cutting both ways for gold: supportive as a hedge but bearish via inflation-driven Fed hikes and higher yields.
insights.quote: long-term yields also rose, primarily driven by fiscal concerns via term premia.
insights.locator: The RMB gold price ended Q3

insights.claim: In early October 2026 gold stabilised, with the RMB gold price hovering around RMB900/gram and the international price holding above US$4,100/oz; geopolitical tensions and their energy-price impact, inflation expectations and the Fed's rate path are expected to drive short-term moves.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Watch energy prices and Fed hike expectations as the key near-term gold catalysts.
insights.quote: Geopolitical tensions and their impact on energy prices, as well as investor expectations around inflation and the Fed’s future rate path, remain key to gold’s short-term moves.
insights.locator: Heading into Q4, gold stabilised

themes.theme: Chinese gold ETFs on record pace

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs added 11t in September 2026, their third consecutive monthly rise, taking total holdings to a month-end record of 304t, though AUM fell 2% to RMB276bn (US$41bn) as the RMB11bn inflow was offset by the lower gold price.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese investors bought the September dip, adding tonnage even as prices fell.
insights.quote: Total holdings reached 304t, a month-end record.
insights.locator: Chinese gold ETF demand persisted

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs recorded inflows of RMB27bn (US$3.9bn) in Q3 2026, lifting quarterly AUM by 13% and holdings by 27t, more than offsetting Q2 outflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Q3 reversed Q2's losses and re-established Chinese ETFs as a major source of investment demand.
insights.quote: Inflows of RMB27bn (US$3.9bn) were recorded in Q3, lifting the quarter’s total AUM by 13% and holdings by 27t.
insights.locator: Inflows of RMB27bn (US$3.9bn) were recorded

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETF demand in Q3 2026 was driven by portfolio diversification amid plunging local equities, lower opportunity costs as Chinese government bond yields kept declining, and encouragement from the PBoC's continuous gold buying announcements.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Weak domestic equities and falling bond yields form a structural tailwind for Chinese gold investment demand.
insights.quote: Demand in Q3 has been influenced by rising portfolio diversification needs in the face of plunging local equities.
insights.locator: Inflows of RMB27bn (US$3.9bn) were recorded

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs' year-to-date inflows are on course for a record year in 2026, and buying continued into early October as local investors diversified amid sustained equity market weakness.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A record ETF year would underpin Chinese investment demand even as jewellery remains weak.
insights.quote: setting Chinese gold ETFs’ y-t-d inflows on course for a record year
insights.locator: Inflows of RMB27bn (US$3.9bn) were recorded

insights.claim: In September 2026 average daily gold futures trading volume on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) fell 9% m/m to 360t/day and net longs of the top 20 participants fell 5t to 149t, reflecting softer sentiment as gold prices and volatility eased.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Speculative Chinese positioning cooled modestly but from elevated levels.
insights.quote: The average daily trading volume on the SHFE contracted 9% m/m to 360t/day
insights.locator: Gold futures market activity cooled

insights.claim: Over Q3 2026, SHFE gold futures net longs held by the top 20 participants surged 59% and trading volumes rose 18%, driven mainly by improving gold price performance after Q2, particularly in August.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese speculative positioning is momentum-driven, so price weakness could unwind some of the 149t net long.
insights.quote: Despite September’s retreat, net longs surged 59% in Q3 while volumes rose 18% during the quarter.
insights.locator: Despite September’s retreat, net longs surged

insights.claim: Gold withdrawals from the Shanghai Gold Exchange (SGE) were 92t in September 2026, up 48% m/m on seasonal pre-National Day jewellery restocking and the price pullback, but still 22% lower y/y and subdued versus historical norms.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The seasonal bounce masks a structurally weaker Chinese jewellery market.
insights.quote: withdrew 92t of gold from the SGE in September, up 48% m/m
insights.locator: Banks, jewellers and other market participants

insights.claim: China's wholesale gold demand totalled 234t in Q3 2026, down 21% y/y and 44% below the ten-year average of 418t, with persistently weak jewellery consumption the main drag.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese physical consumer demand is far below trend at high prices, a key weak spot for global gold demand.
insights.quote: Wholesale gold demand in China totalled 234t in Q3, down 21% y/y and 44% below the ten-year average of 418t.
insights.locator: Wholesale gold demand in China totalled

insights.claim: Anecdotal evidence suggests Chinese bullion sales improved in September 2026 as investors viewed lower prices as a better entry point, with plunging local equities limiting alternatives and PBoC purchase announcements bolstering the search for safe assets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese retail investment demand is price-sensitive and buys dips, partly signalled by central bank behaviour.
insights.quote: Plunging local equities presented Chinese investors with limited options and fired their quest for safe assets
insights.locator: Banks, jewellers and other market participants

insights.claim: During the Mid-Autumn Festival weekend (25-27 September 2026) and the National Day Holiday (1-7 October 2026), demand for gold jewellery, bars and coins notably improved as pre-holiday price pullbacks encouraged dip buying.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Q4 Chinese consumer demand started on a firmer footing thanks to lower prices.
insights.quote: saw demand for gold jewellery, bars and coins notably improve as price pullbacks ahead of the holidays encouraged dip buying
insights.locator: Looking ahead

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects current macro conditions to remain supportive for Chinese bullion investment and Q4's traditional peak season to boost jewellery consumption, though affordability issues and low consumer confidence may keep weighing on tonnage demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Expect investment demand to outperform jewellery in China in Q4, with jewellery tonnage still constrained by high prices.
insights.quote: affordability issues and low consumer confidence may continue to weigh on tonnage demand.
insights.locator: Looking ahead

insights.claim: The People's Bank of China reported a 23t gold purchase in September 2026, its largest monthly buy since October 2023, bringing official holdings to 2,410t, or 8.5% of total reserves, which fell 2% to US$3.8tn mainly due to lower foreign exchange assets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The PBoC is stepping up, not slowing, its reserve diversification into gold.
insights.quote: September’s addition brings China’s official gold holdings to 2,410t, 8.5% of total reserves
insights.locator: Chinese central bank ramped up gold purchases

insights.claim: The PBoC's reported gold buying streak reached 23 consecutive months in September 2026, with Q3 purchases of 63t the strongest quarter since Q3 2023 and year-to-date additions of 103t, making it one of the most active central bank gold buyers globally.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Persistent official demand provides a structural floor for gold prices.
insights.quote: September extended the official sector’s gold accumulation streak to 23 months and pushed the Q3 total to 63t, the strongest quarter since Q3’23.
insights.locator: September extended the official sector’s gold

insights.claim: The PBoC accelerated its gold buying in the face of a declining gold price, suggesting it acts as a price-insensitive or counter-cyclical buyer that adds more on dips.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Price pullbacks may draw larger official purchases, dampening downside.
insights.quote: The PBoC continued with robust gold buying in face of a declining gold price
insights.locator: Chart 5

insights.claim: The PBoC's non-stop gold purchase announcements act as a signal that encourages Chinese private investors to buy gold ETFs and bullion.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Official buying has a second-order effect of amplifying domestic retail and institutional gold demand.
insights.quote: further bolstered by the PBoC’s non-stop gold purchase announcements
insights.locator: Banks, jewellers and other market participants
